Another sick animal... and Aaliyah told you to come to me with this urgently? Hm, this is worrying indeed.
This disease isn't natural, I'm afraid.
We need to track the source of these horrific acts, or it could affect us all... and even reach the city!
Search for clues throughout the mountain ranges and near water sources.
While you look, hold this coin in your palm. It's imbued with a spell that makes it heat up when you're near a strong , tainted source.
If you find anything, come back to me immediately.
It appears that you have successfully tracked down the source of the disease, though I cannot begin to fathom how the aqueducts could have become tainted when they are so heavily guarded.
Someone, or something, must be capable of slipping past the Pyrmos mercenaries unnoticed.
We will also be barred access, as the governor has hired the Pyrmos to keep any of the local factions away from such an important piece of Night Harbor's power struggle.
We will simply have to appeal to the morals of one of the mercenaries posted there. Did you encounter a guard posted at the aqueduct gates themselves?
Uh? What's this, then?
Sounds like your Almina friend already knows that I can't let you inside, but you're also lucky that you brought this to me instead of someone else.
The Pyrmos would take offense to any notion that we're failing in our duties, but being stationed at the gateway means I've heard the things that crawl around in the night.
There are eerie chants and cackles from the crags here at night. Very goblin-like cackles, if you get me.
I can assure you that nothing gets through this gateway, but I wouldn't be surprised if those Muggrah scamps found a hidden passage on the other side of the mountain.

The Bloodynose clan nearby are too scrawny and occupied with their war against the ashira clans, while the Muggrah camp just beyond our keep is always under our watchful eye, so I wouldn't be worried about that one.
No, if I were a betting woman, I'd say that the goblins on the other side of the mountain in the Glass Flats were the ones scaling the cliffs and being a nuisance.
You can go tell your Almina friend that I said as much.
Goblins? What motivation would they have to infect the city's water supply? The goblin clans are typically drawn toward acts of greed, not sheer malice.

That will have to be an investigation for another day, I suppose. If the goblin shamans truly are scaling the mountains and infecting the city's water with their magics, we'll need to create a remedy to counteract it.

The Muggrah shamans and spiritualists derive their power from covetous forces that they link to their personal possessions. You will have to relieve the shamans of a number of these possessions, so that I can develop a counteragent to deliver back to Night Harbor.

Take this satchel and do what you must to fill it with the shaman's trinkets. I am not sure what they currently use, be it beads, fetishes, or some other token, but you must fill the satchel all the same.
Return the filled satchel to me as soon as you can!
Coins? I suppose I should not be surprised, given the goblins' beliefs.
You did well, . Allow me a moment to confer with the spirits on how to best counter this form of magical disease.

Bring this back to Aaliyah so she can treat the waters flowing in from the aqueducts. This is only a temporary solution, but it should at least be sufficient in preventing any further spread of the disease into Night Harbor.
Thank you, , and may Krivea guide your journey.
You're back! What did I tell you? I knew Almina would know what to do!
I'll see that this remedy gets delivered straight to the aqueduct's tenders. How bizarre that the goblin clans were involved in all of this.
We may have to look further into that another day, but for now, you're due for a reward for all your efforts.
Take this token to Calaada just above. I believe she wants to have a word with you.
I'm told you went to great lengths to seek out what was plaguing our water supplies, .
I'm both thankful and honored to have you as a member of the Circle of Scarce Rains. Please, accept this dousing rod so you may continue to bring fresh waters to all those who require it.
In the future we may call upon your services once more, but until then, you're free to set out on whichever journey Krivea has laid out for you.

lines.text: Read Torn Note you start with as a new Enchanter character
Give Torn Note to Master Wincog.
Well, it's good to meet you. Or at least I think it is.
As a novice enchanter, you're required by law to register with the city...though, you could always choose to set your own course. You have a big decision to make.
If you want to be a good, law-abiding citizen, seek out Registrar Vauquelin inside the Spellbinders Spire. He keeps a watchful eye on all registered enchanters.
His office is on the ground level of the Spire, near the entrance. So, if you happen to use the wizards' teleporter, head downstairs.
Give him his registration form. With it, you'll be properly registered.
Or...should you choose otherwise, you can just return it to me. The choice is yours.
Since you're handing me this, I take it you're not looking for work as an entertainer.
You'll likely come to know that being an unregistered enchanter isn't exactly an easy life... but as long as they think you're only capable of party tricks, they tend to leave you alone.
Now, how about you run some errands for me so that my dear friend Nerlbus can take a break? When you're done, I might let you in on a great secret!
Take this robe, bag, and the items to be delivered.
Once you've got the robe and bag on and adjusted, let me know that you're ready to get started.
I'm ready for my instructions
Oh... I'm not sure you're ready for this.
We enchanters are feared by the authorities for a reason. We can appear as anything, or disappear altogether... and, we have the power to get inside the heads of others.
IF YOU WISH TO ENTER THE HOUSE OF CANDOR, YOU MUST KNOW THE CONSEQUENCES OF BETRAYAL!
Well... enough of that.
The deliveries are labeled. Take the first item to Bieito Brightsmile in the Travelers Ward.
Don't worry I'll help you find it.
Here's what he requested in exchange.
Tell ol' Wincog that I appre...
You can find Mirembe in the harbor district. She supervises a warehouse on the waterfront. Go to her at once.
...ciate him finding this for us. We've been all over and inquired to no avail. Thankfully, Wincog's reputation as a procurer precedes him.
Well, take care, and thanks again.
Thanks the gods! I've been waiting for this.
Here's what I found for the trade. I'm happy to get rid of this creepy thing.
They said they found it on one of the islands off the coast, like he said they would.
I don't know what those little ones want with such a thing...
Okay, now head north to the Concourse of Souls. It's built into the mountains that border the city. You'll find Malory in the library there.
I forget what I was saying... but thank you for the delivery, and for taking that creepy thing away from here.
Ah yes... I was expecting you, .
I look forward to reading this. It's very rare, but Master Wincog has an impeccable ability to acquire peculiar things... take you, for example.
Well, I'm sure you'll turn out fine.
Your master should know better than to try entering my mind. It's a fine parlor trick, but we're quite heavily warded here.
Here's the gift I promised the gnome. After that little stunt he just pulled, I should keep it, but then you'd be unable to finish your task.
Oh, and he wants you to give the last package to Sexton Harding. You can find him in the old cemetery outside of the Northern Gate. There's a shortcut to it through the Black Feather Bazaar.
Since you're heading there, you may need this.
Best of luck!
Oh! Oh dear... this is a surprise. I'd entirely forgotten about it!
Don't worry, don't worry... the skull isn't from here. I wouldn't dare defile this sacred garden. It was brought onto the grounds by some ne'er-do-wells who didn't belong here.
Well, they're occupying their own spaces here now. Buried proper-like. Got 'em both with my pickaxe and shovel, whilst they were neck-deep in someone else's grave.
Master Wincog said that if I were ever to come across a skull with these markings, we'd have a trade to make. Sure enough, the robbers had one in their bag.
But, I'd completely forgotten about it until now! It's lucky that you came by!
Take 'im that skull, and my thanks. No idea how he knew it'd be here, but there it is... and here's my moth cage!
I appreciate the help. I hope you enjoyed yourself and made some new friends.
You're going to meet a few more people, or at least, mostly people, as part of your next journey.
Take this key to the Grand Library in Sageside. It's big, so you can't miss it.
If you're clever, you'll find a secret lair in which your new allies reside!
If you're not so clever, you'll be surrounded by books for hours and hours, so maybe you'll eventually become clever enough to figure it out.
Now, go to the library and show that key to Vaclav. He'll take care of you from here.
Welcome to the House of Candor! We've been expecting your arrival, Master Wincog was quite eager for us to meet.
Night Harbor is still growing, so you may find that we'll occupy a different location in the future. For now, please enjoy our facility here.
...Oh! You gave me your key, you'll need that back.
Now... where was I? Ah, yes! The House of Candor is a distributed collective, which means you can find us throughout the realms of Aêthoril.
To preserve our order and, thereby, our personal safety, we excel at acquiring knowledge, making deals, and generally being indispensable.
What knowledge?
We can be quite persuasive, so the House has often been called upon to assist with important negotiations... or to gather information to gain the upper hand in such matters.

Do not worry! If you have more of a taste for flash and danger, there's ample opportunity to assist bold adventurers heading into the hither or dither. Personally, though, I'll have none of that. I'd prefer to simply sit here and read.
Welcome! It's nice to see a new face.
That's a joke. We're enchanters, we constantly see new faces... even on the same people.
If Vaclav just sent you, then you probably need more practice before you can assist us. Once you're ready, speak with the twins, Pau and Piia. They'll likely have a job for you.
Oh, and be sure to keep the key with you at all times. You never know when you'll need it.
Very well, if you're ready to assist us, let's get to it.
First of all, here's your key back.
We've learned of a shipment arriving via some smugglers who operate from a cove west of the city.
Pay them a visit. Look inside their tents to see if you can find a small, ironbound crate. However, if you do find it, don't open it. It's very dangerous.

It's bound for a person of great importance here in the city, so it's likely to be well-hidden until they're ready to smuggle it in. Be sure to inspect anything that seems out of the ordinary within those tents.
Once you've retrieved it, bring it to Jamee Langris. You'll find him where the bards meet to perform in the Night Market.
Good luck.
Oh dear, this is quite a surprise! The twins must have sent you.
I wasn't certain whether the rumors of its existence were true, but we'll find out soon enough.
My client will be very, very pleased. In return, please accept this gift to take to Piia.
Well done! Jamee said he'd be able to find this for me. It's a study of human behaviour under stress, written by the physicians of Lymian. Pau and I are quite eager to learn.
In exchange, I offer you this.
Please accept it as a token of my appreciation.
Take care now, though do visit later. I may have another favor to ask of you.
Braided Crystal Ring

There, now you are properly registered.
You are required by law to wear this robe, as it signifies your registration status with the authorities. Do not dispose of it.
Smart choice. As you likely know, being an unregistered enchanter isn't exactly an easy life... But as long as they think you're only capable of party tricks, they tend to leave you alone.
Now, since you went and registered, you'll need to make an effort to regain the trust of House Candor.
How about you run some errands for me so that my dear friend Nerlbus can take a break? When you're done, I'll put in a good word for you.
They're still using that same old scrying spell to track registrants. It's highly inaccurate and easy to remove.
Here, put on this bag along with your disenchanted robe. Also, take these items for delivery.
Once you've got them on, let me know that you're ready to go. When you're done, return the filled bag and your robe to me.

Unfortunately, it might be weeks before I can file your application. Mother has tasked me with important research, so I'm very busy. Unless...

What took yo uso long? Did Elrind send you on one of his scavenger hunts? Never mind. Don't keep me waiting again.

We practice in the garrison, but true training occurs in the field. And this is where the Steel Talons excel.
That's why our most promising members are sought after by the Night Harbor Guard or the Red Mantles.

The Ashira have been harassing the city's borders and this is as good as an opportunity as ever to support the efforts of the Night Harbor Guard and the Red Mantles, and to distinguish yourself as a competent member of the Steel Talons.

lines.text: This quest begins in the Underdocks western district inside an inn on the southern rise by speaking with Innkeeper Farda.
Hail, Innkeeper Farda.
I have good food and safe rooms. Coins are paid up front for a stay or a meal. And keep your animals outside.
That includes Goblins.
Why do you dislike Goblins?
They make a mess and only cause trouble. I don't work to lose money.
I want some food
The dining room is on the second floor. Just head up those stairs behind me and you will smell the food at the top.
I want a room
Take a look for yourself. Downstairs rooms if you have fewer coin and upstairs if you have more.
And do not mind the current layout. The building next door was a... recent acquisition
Tell me about your recent acquisition
The tenants next door fell on hard times. I took on their debt and now this entire building is mine.
Innkeeper Farda doesn't have much else to share. Head upstairs and chat with Barkeeper Tull.
Hail, Barkeeper Tull.
Yes, hail to you too. I haven't much time since I'm ferrying plates up and down these stairs all day.
Why are you ferrying plates up and down these stairs all day?

It wasn't so bad before Farda kicked those gnomes out of the unit next door. The kitchen used to be so close, but more rooms to sleep means more coins to keep, so now I'm burning my legs going up and down all day.
Who were the gnomes?
Bad business that. But Farda had her eye on that unit for a while.
They always thought they could make it big bringing shroom wood above ground but... well, we see how that went.
Tull does not provide much more information, but he does respond to inquiries about his colleagues.
Who is Farda?
She owns this inn. Not much humor in her, but she keeps me well employed.
Head outside into the adjacent building and speak with Chef Brigit
Hail, Chef Brigit.
Are you lost? You don't look like a new server. This is my kitchen and I don't need you sneaking a taste of my meals.
I am a new server
Why don't you go in the other entrance and talk to Farda. She can help you.
She runs this place. If you need a room, go speak with her. And don't try to bargain with her or she'll raise the prices on you.
Off with you now, shoo!
Tell me about Barkeeper Tull
Where is that rascal? I have three meals waiting to go upstairs.

Who is Brigit?
You'll find her in the kitchen. I try not to spend much time there. It gets too hot for me.

lines.text: Hail, Reeve Thurston Winter
Greeting. I am Reeve Thurston Winter, charged with keeping order in Penshaw.
These are hard times, and what peace we have left is easilyt broken. We have opened our doors to capale outsiders willing to help us face a growing threat.
What outside threat?
The Sangrel Fist has become a scourge on our roads and farms. They are ruthless thieves emboldened by their numbers, who prey on honest folk who can scarcely defend themselves.
We cannot allow this to continue. Seek them out and then their ranks. They wear red wraps upon their hands. Bring me four as proof.
You certainly did your part. Well done. The Sangrel Fist has brought enough fear to this village. Perhaps they'll think twice before entering our gates.
Every bandit brought down is one less threat to oue farms and homes.
Take this sigil. Carrying it authorizes you to privileged information, should be needed to defend Penshaw.
Hail, Detective Brunsworth.
Hail, Adventurer, and well met. I have heard good things about your services in Penshaw.
I was sent here to investigate the growing threat of the Sangrel. Their numbers have sharply increased as of late. Perhaps you would be willing to dig a little further for us?
I will dig a little further.
Very good. We know little of what binds these cult bandits together.
This type of organization requires leadership. Go to their camps and search for clues. Whether found among their belongings or taken from those who carry them matters little.
/inspect crate
/take scroll
How interesting... This text seems to be written in an old tongue.

We will need an expert to translate its meaning. The abbey outside of Penshaw is home to scribes versed in fortgotten tongues. Seek their aid, and when you return with their translation, present your sigil as well so you may be properly rewarded.
This appears to be doctrine... a structure set of rites meant to be memorized by initiates of this cult. It attracts the sort who would rather blame fate than earn an honest living.
This is no reason to assume any truth in it. If Eyzin has followers, it is because he is persuasive, or because he understands how to manipulate desperate men.
Their success is far more likely to be practical than divine. Spies within the town, watches along the roads, or a vantage point over our docks. That is where we find answers, not in fire and ash.
I will gather further intelligence. This investigation is not concluded.
For now, you have proven capable. Take this. It is a sigil for one worthy of your skill, granted in recognition of your diligence.

lines.text: The miners are already grumbling that there's not enough chow.
Hmmm, I think I have an idea that will solve one of our problems and fill our bellies at the same time.
What food?
Yes, we need more food. I've had to portion out our rations since the shipment is late... but I think I've got an idea that could help us out...
What idea?
Have ya ever had steam crab legs fresh out of the harbor? Delicious aren't they?
Well, I've been think'... maybe, just maybe, these cinder beetles are kinda like those crabs.
Bring me six tender beetle legs and I'll try cookin' them up for the crew.
You know how to tell if the legs will be tender, don't ya?
How will I tell if they'll be tender?
Yes, Yes, it must be tender meat. Old meat is too tough.
I'd look for cinder beetles that are younger... smaller... the hardest workers in the swarm. Their legs will have plenty of meat on 'em.
Give Foreman Stonehammer six Tender Beetle Legs. They drop off a cinder worker.
Yes, this will do perfectly. Wait here a moment.
This is delicious! Ya ought t' try it. Here, and a few copper for your troubles.
You receive 2x Boiled Beetle Legs from Foreman Stonehammer.
Hail, Captain Hale.
You've picked a fine day to be poking around. You might be able to help me, though. We're in a bit of a bind.
I can help.
The storm that blew through last night shook part of the cargo load loose, and the Harbormaster's already been warning us that if we don't recover it, it'll be a disaster.
We're waiting on our equipment to arrive to we can retrieve it, but my crew feels uneasy about what's been lurking down there. I can't blame them. We all saw their shadows gliding through the waves.
What is lurking?

There's no mistaking it. Great bight sharks have been circling the shallows. Regardless, the cargo was heavy and wouldn't have floated too far. Whatever went over would've settled on the seabed just offshore.
We estimate we've lost at least five creates. If you're willing to brave the water and bring them back, I'll see you paid for the trouble.

Good work, Almond! Anything left out there will be split or dragged out by tomorrow. You saved what could be saved. Here, as promised, take this for doing us a solid favor. My crew already looks relieved.

lines.text: Begin heading to Jaffar Jhaym
Hand Rune-Etched Note to Jaffar Jhaym.
Very well met! You have arrived safely, and I am indeed who you seek. Welcome to the Spellbinders Spire!
The desert grows more dangerous by the day, so you have arrived none too soon.
I am sure we will get better acquainted in the days to come, but you must be tired, so I’ll delay your introduction to your trainer no longer.
As an aspiring inquisitor, you will be under the tutelage of Petra Gyle.
Deliver your note to her, and she will get you started.
Head down the spire and hand your Rune-Etched Note "Petra Gyle" to Petra Gyle.
Hmm...
So you wish to be an inquisitor of the spire, do you? You'll have to prove to me you have the mettle to take on such a responsibility.
Magic is a powerful, yet extremely dangerous talent. Especially when used by those who collude with, or seek to benefit from, corrupted forces.
Our role as inquisitors is to protect our colleagues from such forces, while also routing out corruption before it has a chance to take hold.
Are you prepared to take on this role?
Yes I am.
We shall see if there's truth to your words, or if they ring hollow.
Descend to the bottom floor of the Spire and use the key I've given you to enter the confinement cells. We've captured a number of cultists that have yet to reveal to us their intentions.
Even a novice like yourself should have the aptitude to force them to talk.
Speak to the Inquisitor Selpha outside the cells should you have any questions regarding interrogation, then return to me with anything you uncover, along with the key to the cells.
Head down the confinement cells and hold your Spellbinder's Cell Key and click the cell door next to Inquisitor Selpha.
Cast Torment on one of the prisoners three times, they will then tell you about a secret pocket in their cloaks.
There will be a table with some knives on it in the room outside. /Look at the table, then /inspect cloak, then /inspect seam, then /take note. Give it to Inquisitor Selpha.
What's this? You found this hidden within one of their cloaks? Hmm...
You'd best show these to Petra right away. The spike carries a malevolent aura that she may be able to unravel, along with the meaning behind that blank note.
Return to Petra Gyle, and give her the Mysterious Rolled Note, the Mysterious Iron Spike and the Spellbinder's Cell Key.
You did well to bring these finds to me, Name, while also proving that you have the resolve to be a true inquisitor.
Take this, it will serve as a symbol that you're now a member of our order. You'll need it, along with this seer stone, if you're to look further into these matters.
Tell me, Name, are you familiar with the Tarellian Seer Stones?
What Seer Stones?
The seer stone that I've given you is magically imbued. It enables us to see through minor illusions and masking spells, which is how you'll use it to thwart the cultists.
These so-called spikes have been revealed to scrying anchors. They would allow anyone attuned to them to view, and potentially overhear, anything in their vicinity.
I've also used the power of the Tarellian Seer Stone to dispel the illusion concealing what information the note contained.
It appears that out Easthymnite guests have been directed to discreetly affix these spikes at various locations throughout Night Harbor, likely in an effort to spy and sow discord.
So now, Name, to continue your investigations you must make a choice.
What choice?
Path Choice

Your first option is to pursue the cultists that have been sent to plant these spikes, either by following them or discerning the clues revealed in the note about their intended locations. For this, you'll need the note.

The second option is to track down and eliminate the individual who is attuned to the spikes, so that even if they're planted, they'll remain nothing more than a potential snag on someone's clothing. To do this, you'll require the spike.
As this is your first investigation, I leave the choice to you, Name.
Note or spike?
Give me the note.
Very well, the note is yours.
You receive Revealed Cultist Note.

There are three travelers from Easthymn who've caught our eye at the Shaded Bloom Inn. You'll recognize them by their black garb and the thin silver chains they wear around their waists. Identify them and follow them.

Two of them have been reported to wander the streets, making brief stops at nondescript locations. With the seer stone, look closely at the areas where they stop. You're to pull out any spikes they affix to these locations.
You may be able to use the note to discern the locations yourself without having to following them, if you're keen enough.

The third traveler never leaves the inn, but we're not sure why. Follow him as well, but if he doesn't affix the spikes anywhere... take them from him. The spire authorizes the use of force, once he is out of sight of the locals.
Fill the bag with each unique spike, combine it, and then return it to me, along with the seer stone.
Head to the Shaded Bloom Inn near the west gate.
Hand the Tarellian Seer Stone and Small Bag of Spikes to Petra Gyle.
Well done. You've returned, so I must assume you were able to trail them safely.
Oh, did you get into a tussle?.
Seems you can handle a more direct challenge then.
We're tasked with tracking down and dealing with mages, wizards, and other arcane filth. However, we are also charged, at times, to deal with adversaries of a more spiritual nature.
Seek out two camps in the desert to the west. There are shamans amongst the Ashira. Gather medicinal herbs from them to replenish the first pouch.

You'll find a group of smugglers along the coast. They work for Jens Vermahn, so take care to engage them during the day. Gather whatever leafy filth they're using to heal themselves in the second bag.
Now go.
Spike
The spike is yours, then.
If you're going to find out who has attuned themselves to the spike, you'll need the assistance of another member of our order.
Bring the spike to Spellbinder Kharash. I imagine he'll be in the archives on the bottom floor, opposite the hallway where you found the containment cells.
He's an expert at unraveling divination magics and will be able to help you trace its origin.
Good hunting, Name.
You bring me a cursed object, inquisitor. I sense foul magics tied to it... divine in origin. Likely a dark gift granted by a malevolent benefactor.
In the meanwhile, take this bag. You must fill it With the components I need to trace the magic of the spike back to its source.
what components?
Good of you to ask.
The components I need to seek this foe rely on the vision of those who scour the sands. You must acquire the eye of a bat, a fire beetle, a dune scarab, a spiderling, and a crypt scarab.
I will also need a mirror to reflect the gaze back to its source. I believe Haredi sells such trinkets to other students of the academy in the Grand Library.
Once you have an of the eyes and the mirror, combine them in the bag and return it to me. I Will then conduct the ritual to reverse the attunement Of the spike.
Take it, Drixquist. I have reversed the attunement of the object and directed the eyes to assist you in locating the cultist leader.
There is now one final thing you must do.
What must I do?
Before you depart, you must be sure to bring your Tarellian Seer Stone with you.
When you are ready, proceed down to the Northern Gate. While standing beneath it, focus your will into the spike and it shall conjure an eye that will lead you to the cultist scryer.
If an eye does not immediately appear, the villain may be momentarily out of sight. Simply wait a short moment before trying once again.
When an eye appears, follow it. After that, you must use your own judgment on how best to deliver the Spellbinder's justice to your foe.
Bring anything you find from you investigation back to Petra, as my part here has concluded. May Tilustra illuminate path, inquisitor.
No! How did you...?
Your blood will serve as a sacrifice for Kravvin!
Well done. It seems you may have what it takes to be a real inquisitor after all.
Oh, did you get into a tussle?.
Seems you can handle a more direct challenge then.
We're tasked with tracking down and dealing with mages, wizards, and other arcane filth. However, we are also charged, at times, to deal with adversaries of a more spiritual nature.
Seek out two camps in the desert to the west. There are shamans amongst the Ashira. Gather medicinal herbs from them to replenish the first pouch.

You'll find a group of smugglers along the coast. They work for Jens Vermahn, so take care to engage them during the day. Gather whatever leafy filth they're using to heal themselves in the second bag.
Now go.
Hand the filled Ashira Herb Pouch and Filthy Leather Herb Pouch to Petra Gyle.
Fantastic Work. We've been using these herbs to formulate a better understanding of how to disrupt the enemy's healing magics.
The spiritual nature of Ashira magic is more challenging to understand, but Jens' rats appear to be using simple alchemy. We'll know soon enough.
Well, young recruit, you're proving to be quite the find. I've got one last task, then we'll let you get some rest.
I've just been made aware of a powerful, yet still up-in-coming wizard, in league with Jens. He can occasionally be found in a small house in the Bends.
You're to kill him and bring me his head. Pack it in this bag so you don't draw any unwanted attention.
Head to the Bends part of Night Harbor. There is a teleporter just before north bank that will take you to the shipyard area. Take the teleporter and go left to get to the Bends.
Kill Sahir Muzalal and loot his Bloodied Wizard Head.
Head back to Petra Gyle.
Hand the filled Rune Covered Black Silk Bag to Petra Gyle.
Good work. He was on his way to becoming a powerful adversary, so it benefits us to be rid of him.

For now, consider yourself well on your way down the proper path. Continue to explore the city and familiarize yourself with the people here. If you run into anything suspicious, come back to me. Otherwise, get some rest.
And keep this with you.

lines.text: This quest starts with hailing Mar'Tem.
Hail, Yes, I speak your language, though I am the only one in our gathering who does.
We mean no harm to your kind. In fact, we are the ones who fear harm. We have fled to this shelter to escape the hunters tracking us.
The undead here have done well to keep them in the tunnel but it is only a matter of time before they come for us.
What hunters?
A group of us were able to flee the Skri'Var taskmasters before they could cause us to degenerate.
We escaped here, but if the hunters leave, we will eventually make our way out of this place and return to our village.
Or, if you can force them away, we would also be grateful. Just bring me proof that you have dealt with them.
Degenerate?

The Skri'Var were once like us Mur'Hua. But those with bad spirits wander away from our people and devolve into what you see here. We take care of each other, and we love to explore and create. They are selfish and kill and steal.
They can force us to become like them by isolating us from each other, torturing us, and making us cannibals like them.
Once this process beings, our spirits change and our minds give way. We serve them, protect them, and become like them. So, take care if you see any Mur'Hua among them. They are already likely lost.
What Village?
We come from a small village on a lake deep below the surface... but I do not know you well enough to tell you more.
What proof?
It is a shame that one of our own can cause so much death and hardship. We are immensely grateful for this act of kindness.
Please take this as a small token of my gratitude. It may help you, should you encounter more of my people.

Now... move along citizen, if you please.
You've done more than carry cloth today. You helped an old ogre keep her promises.
That matters. Words matter. Keeping your word matters a lot in cities like this one. A few words from the right person can change lives.
Speaking of words and promises...this here's a sakk. Good as tender with merchants in Night Harbor. This one is for tailoring services.
I was going to choose something for myself. Thought I might need it.
But I think it'll suit you better than it ever would me.
Now there's a choice you have to make, lily.
Do you want a shirt or a robe?
Part 2A, if you want a shirt
Well now! You truly went and found them. Excellent!
Thank you for returning this to me. My uncle was a kind man. I was very young when he passed away. My aunt passed not too long after that.
I was brought to the Wayfarers Hospice and raised by Sojourners. The key was given to me later by the priests of Relle.
Right then! The sakk covers my labor and you've brought the materials. Stand back just a moment. Let me see what we can make of this.
There we are. One crude silk shirt. It's dirty and won't turn any heads in Highpoint Terrace, but it'll serve you well enough.

All you need to do now is wash it. Head down to the water in the harbor, near my uncle's house. There are some scullery maidens washing and drying the clothes. Tell them Noura sent you, and they'll show you what you need to do next.
Part 2B if you want a robe
Yes? How may I help you?
I will honor it.
No.
The sakk, of course, is for the work, not the weave.
Crude silk, not the fine kind scholars preen over, mind you. Common silk. Resourceful, durable, and resilient, much like those priests of Porbor.
I have six crude silk scraps here, but will need twelve to finish a robe.
Keep the sakk for now. Since my crude silk stock is low, you will have to wait until I find more.
Yes. Crude. Specifically, crude silk scraps.
Crude silk comes from cobweavers. You know, the tiny spiders no bigger than my thumb. Hardly a challenge for a slayer such as yourself.

There is an old house where you might find some. It is abandoned now. The owner passed long ago, and no one has been there in years. It is likely crawling with cobweavers, though, it was locked the last time I passed by.
I knew the family once...well, I was a friend of the girl who lived there.
Never mind. That was long ago.
If you wish to check out the house, let me know. Otherwise, just return later when I have more crude silk in stock.
Oh...you want to check out the house?
When I was a girl, I stayed there often with my friend. We used to gather cobweaver silk from the attic. We made clothes for our dolls from it. Poor sticthes, but we were proud of them.
...But there is a curious barrel along the side of the building, under a torn awning. Always was.
The lid hides a small door we used to sneak through. I think they put it there as a way to cover the hole in the wall without pinching he purse.
We would slip inside at night, then head down to the water to swim in the harbor. If her uncle caught us...well, he never did. He slept like a Scarwood bear in winter and we were quiet as mice.
Good luck. I will see you when you get back. Oh, I almost forgot! You will need this.
Use this to combine four crude silk webs to make the scraps, then return it to me when you have them made.
Yes...these will do nicely. Strong fibers.
Good. Everything is in order.
This will only take a minute or two.
It is dirty and will not turn heads in Highpoint Terracce, but it will server you well, I think.

All you need to do is wash it. Down by the water in the harbor, near the boatwright's house, there are some scullery maids working, washing and dying the clothes. Tell them Mira sent you. They will show you what you need to do next.
Part 3 for either robe or shirt

lines.text: Hand Humble Note to Chahaya Tam
You wish to train with our order?

Welcome to the School of the Fourfold Path, where one can refine their body and mind, and seek a connection with the four elements. I am Master Chahaya Tam, I lead this order, alongside my husband, Tenebrim. You have done well to seek us out, as there are no greater adepts of the pugilist arts within this city than us.

Let's get started. For your initial training, I would like you to approach and challenge some of our students to a sparring match. They will not hold back, and I do not expect you to, either. If they know you down, the match will be over, but you can return to spar later when you have honed your skill. If you have further questions about the matches, just ask about them. All of us in the order have had to pass through this trial by fire, so to speak.

Wear your belt, so they know you as a fellow student, and speak to them to start sparring. Recover a training emblem from them. When you have bested three of our students, return to me, along with your belt. Tran and fight!
Hail a strong sparring monk and say "let's spar", then proceed to defeat 3 of them.
Hand all 3 Training Emblem and your Fourfold Sash to Chahaya Tam
Wonderful! Wasn't it an exhilarating experience? Do not worry, your bruises will heal in time.
Your first victories! I am proud of you and present you with your new belt, marking you as a member of the First Degree.
Wear it with pride,
Now, go and get some training. Once you have a few more matches under your belt, and have spent time with your fellow adventurers, come to me for your next task.
! There you are.
I see a few additional scars... you must have been out training. Good!
We've been honing your physical prowess, but today, you're going to work on another side of yourself. Your mind needs to be one with your body.
We need you to head into the sweltering heat of the Shaded Dunes and find the refreshing Waterfall of Serenity.
Do you feel up to the task? Hand me your belt if so. I'll check it for wear and tear.
I can see you've taken good care of it.
Take this elixir and be on your way. Remember, this is a test of the mind, not the body.
Wonderful, trainee. You've manage to overcome your fears and focus your mind to the limit of its current capabilities!
I'm truly delighted to award yo with the rank of third-degree monk!
It's no small feat for a trainee to have such control, you should be proud of yourself.

lines.text: Hail, Sporeweaver Underveil.
I welcome you to the depths of Sporehaven Karst, [class]. Our myconids are of no threat under normal circumstances, though it appears something has tampered with the latest strain.
Strain?

I cannot say for certain what is causing the aggression in our latest strain, but I do have my suspicion. They seem to get riled when the sun sets and a mysterious foam builds along the riverbanks of the Karst.
Foam?
I have discovered traces of the mysterious foam caught in the gills of some of our myconid children, though I have not yet procured enough to get an understanding of what it truly is.
Should a myconid become enthralled by the substance, they soon begin sending out messages of warning through the nerve structures of their surrounding kin, riling them into a defensive frenzy.
I am loathe to ask this of you, stranger, but I am not strong enough to bring low any of my children. Would you be able to take a stand against my beguiled creations?
I will take a stand.
Then I entrust the deed to you. Seek out my beguiled children here in the Karst; the bluecaps appear to be the most susceptible at night.
Cull what you must to procure a section of their gills that shimmers with traces of the prismatic foam. Bring what you find to me, so I can save what remains of our latest strain.
Collect Prismatic gills from a beguiled bluecap during the night and deliver them to Sporeweaver Underveil.

Such a waste of a beatiful strain. I understand why it had to be done, but this goes against the balance of the Weald. My poor children were never meant to be enthralled by something not of this world.
Which is precisely what this magic resembles... the machinations of the naiads. I had my suspicions, but this evidence you brought me confirms them.
They have tainted the river with their influence. To what end, I care not. I only ask, will you provide me the opportunity to avenge my fallen kin?
I will avenge your fallen kin.
Thank you, stranger. Enter the domain of the naiads and use what force or guile is necessary to reach the pools that dwell within.

Rumors tell of their ability to enthrall beings of pure water. If these rumors hold true, I need you to collect at least four samples of this enchanted water so that I can study it and develop a countermeasure for my own creations.
Do this for me, and you will have the eternal gratitude of the Circle of Spores. I wish you luck, stranger.
Collect 4 Enchanted water from a beguiled water elemental in the naiad cave upstream and combine them in Underveil's phial.

lines.text: You have been summoned to the Concourse of Souls.
Give Weathered Note to Marvion Hallows.

Oh, a new student! This is worth the interruption, well, as long as you don't make a habit of it. I assume you'll be dealing primarily with Buckmarr, Sekhmet, or one of Exavius's people, as I am quite busy.
Given the influx of new students, Sekhmet should be prepared for your arrival. Take your note to him. You'll find him below in the morgue.

Give Weathered Note to Sekhmet who is also in the Concourse of Souls.
Welcome to the Concourse of Souls! As the professor may have mentioned, I am Sekhmet. I will assist you in your studies.

As you can see, we try to keep the morgues well-stocked to accommodate a broad varied range of study. Fortunately, Night Harbor is generous in its donations to our cause... the city produces a lot of dead.

Buckmarr, our alchemist, asked me to gather some materials for him. I genuinely do not enjoy the outdoors, so perhaps you could assist with this? Take this jar and fill it with Incarnal Residue. Eight should do. Then bring it to Buckmarr.
You do know what incarnal residue is, do you not?
Receive Small Clay Jar from Sekhmet.
No. What is incarnal residue?
Excellent question! Incarnal residue is the name that Buckmarr has given a fascinating substance he is researching. He is very fond of giving things new names.

The residue can be found on the bones of reanimated skeletons. Though Buckt disagrees, I believe it manifests most commonly when the skeleton's life, or more accurately, animating energy is drained from its corporeal form through necromantic magic.
Keep that in mind.
Good hunting, and do not forget to give the jar to Buckmarr once it has been filled!
Combine 8 Incarnal Residue in Small Clay Jar to get a filled Small Clay Jar. Hand it to Buckmarr Gorstagg in the Concourse of Souls.
Ahh, you're new. I bet Sekhmet sent you out so he could continue to hide inside. Did he tell you that this was my discovery?
Well, it was. It's just one of many. I have a knack for alchemical advancement. One day, our modest college will be quite renowned at the rate I'm going.
Speaking of renown, you may wear this to formalize your association with our fine school.
Receive Black and Gold Robe from Buckmarr Gorstagg
Now, if you'd like to assist me with another matter, read this list and return it to me along with the materials it describes. These items are vital to my research.
Receive Buckmarr's List from Buckmarr Gorstagg
Except for the pelt, that's a personal matter. I loathe wererats.
Turn in Buckmarr's List along with Wererat Pelt, Corrupted Heart, Ghostly Cloth Scrap, Vibroplasmic Residue
Well, I hope that one suffered.

lines.text: Hand Formal Note to Thibald Burlond in the Wayfarer's Hospice north of the West Gate
Welcome to the Wayfarers Hospice. I am Grand Master Thibald Burdlond of the Penitent Knights of the Hospice.
We accept all paladins who come to aid and maintain our order, no matter their background or faith.
This hospice is known to Night Harbor's citizens and authorities alike as a place of order and charity. Your faith and your history are of no concern, but do not besmirch our good name.
Now, please deliver the note you just gave me to Master Fulton. You will serve his needs.
Hand Formal Note to Trey Fulton
Our Grand Master is a loud enough fella, isn't he?
It's a pleasure to meet you and all that, but let's cut right to it, eh? We've got a lot of work ahead of us.
An increasing number of travelers are coming through our city gates having been wounded or worse. Most tell tales of Ashira ambushes or hordes of undead appearing in the night.
But before we send you to take on the night, I need you to show this coin to Ol' Grimsul at the inn just across the street. This will be your first big mission.
Head to the Inn near the West Gate and hand your Penitent Knight's Coin to Halrinn Grimsul
Well, it's good to see that the old cuss finally found his appetite.
It looks like you've become his courier, brave knight.
But first, you'll need to do the other thing he sent you here for.
As a brave defender of whatever faith you claim to follow, I'm sure my task is a trivial endeavor. I'll need you to kill two birds with one stone, so to speak.
We're short on staff, so I'm stuck up here for a bit while grain beetles gnaw away at our supplies in the cellar. Also, our cook is running low on ingredients for the stew...
You get it, right? Fill the bag with their legs and return it to me. Then you can go back to whatever brave deeds you thought you'd be doing. Just make sure those legs are intact and juicy looking.
Head behind the bar and head to the basement and kill a grain beetles until you receive 6 of them. Alternatively you can buy them.
Hand Bag of Intact Beetle Legs to Halrinn Grimsul
Everyone, my brave defender has returned!
I may jest, but... I do truly appreciate the assistance. Master Fulton's food is wrapped up and ready to go. Deliver it to my dear sir, before it gets cold.
And no, don't worry, it's not the stew.
Do see that he gets this and eats it. I'm glad he finally sent for something. I'll not have him waste away from worry.
The situation with his son is unfortunate, and he's a good man. There's no telling what happened to his son. He was a paladin, like yourself.
I'll not have him starve while waiting on word in the meantime.
Hand Food for Trey Fulton to Trey Fulton
Thank you for this. I assume Halrinn put you to work for it.
Take this for your efforts.
It was good for you to meet, Halrinn. He may tend bar now, but he was formidable in his day. As were many of the people you'll serve here in the hospice and as part of our guild.
This place and our duty, is a constant reminder that time moves swiftly, eluding even the most fastidious grasp.
Ah, look at me getting all morose. Don your tunic and explore the city. I have nothing for you now, but come back soon and we'll put you to work.
Return to the Shaded Bloom Inn near West Gate and ask Halrinn Grimsul about Trey's son
Master Fulton's son, Troy, went on an expedition to investigate the origins of the undead in our area and has yet to return. His son is an experienced paladin, but he's been missing for weeks.
Given all the kindness they showed my brother during his last days in the hospice, I'm compelled to assist however I can... But here I am, my adventuring days behind me.
I overheard a conversation last week between a few inebriated archaeologists from the Wyrmsbane site.
They've been unable to explore the site too deeply due to increased undead activity, but they mentioned seeing what looked like signs of a recent and significant skirmish.
It's not much to go on, so I haven't passed it along. I'd hate to worry Master Fulton without real cause. Please keep this between us, and deliver that food before it gets cold.
Head to the Tomb of the Last Wyrmsbane to search for clues regarding the whereabouts of Trey Fulton's son.
/take coin

Hand Troy's Field Pack to Trey Fulton
By the Gods! This is my son's field pack. These items belong to Troy!
I'd heard rumors that he and his men entered the tomb, but now we have confirmation!
The initiative you've shown is only outdone by your heroism. Remove that trainee tunic and take this with my gratitude. You're clearly deserving of a more permanent role here.
He may have lost his gear, but he's still alive. I can feel it.
I'm going to speak with Grand Master Burlond about the appropriate course of action. In the meantime, please let me know if you see any signs of my son while you're beyond the gates.

Willing to aid your cause

Your resolve honors our cause, Druid. The poachers wield skinning knives etched with their foul mark. Bring me four of them as proof of your deed, and I shall reward your service. May the forests' will guide you.

samples

Ah, nevermind! Here it is.
The ample sample list is as follows... four pieces of pyrite ore, three clear crystal shards, two smoky shards, and a flawless clear quartz.
Place the minerals in this case and seal it, then bring the case and note back to me. A full case of minerals means a full payout in coin! Good luck!
Good... no, splendid work!
Well then, a reward is in order. Take this as a token of appreciation from the Church of Trem.

steps.text: Hand in 1 x Request for Aid to Captain Relgen Greenblade.
You receive Evidence of Orcs.
You receive Evidence of Nymphs.
You receive Evidence of Sporehaven.
You receive Scintillating Page.

lines.text: Hail, Captain Relgen Greenblade.
I have no mind for idle talk, unless you've something important to share.
Hand in 1 x Request for Aid to Captain Relgen Greenblade.
Ah, a new volunteer? Let me get a look at you, then.
You look like you'll do. I am Relgen Greenblade, Regional Captain of the Ardent Keepers, and it's my duty to safeguard our borders from all threats within and without.
As the request mentioned, we're in need of fresh rangers who are willing to maintain a presence in Evershade Weald, and to that end, I would see that you're put to work immediately.
Are you prepared, ranger?
I am prepared.

Good. Being as fresh as you are, I'll not yet have you engage priority threats. Your first mission will be one of reconnaissance and familiarizing yourself with the forest's layout. Our rangers need to know their way around, after all.
You'll investigate three locations within the Weald, then report your findings and any evidence you find in the logbook.
If you can return with a full logbook of useful information, you'll have proven that you're worthy of being inducted into the Ardent Keepers as a formal initiate.

As for the locations, you'll be reporting on the Whispering Pools, Sporehaven Karst, and a ruined archway that spans the border of Keepers Bight. You need only ask if you require further details on each of these locations.
I'll remind you that you are to look closely at each site and report your findings. You are not there to take action. These places are still dangerous for a prospective ranger.
What are the Whispering Pools?
Devious naiads make the Whispering Pools their home. They reside behind the great falls of the river that splits the Weald in two.
Be warned, the Fossergrim you'll encounter may be peaceful enough, but the nymphs who dwell further inside are known to possess travelers and keep them as playthings.

Don't venture too deep inside. In fact, make your report from inside the cave's mouth, just past the threshold of the falls. I must know if there are any signs that they're attempting to breach their pact and leave the caves.
Their pact?

It's my opinion that the fae in general cannot be trusted, even if bound to a pact. The naiads are no exception. Their mistress, Naelira, is bound to the pools of that cave, but I fear she wishes to expand her influence.
Who is Naelira?
Enough of the fae! Just speaking of them makes my ears burn. If you want to learn more about them, you should consult the Heartwood Archives.
Where are the Heartwood Archives?
The Heartwood Archives is Faelindral's great library, kept by the Preservers. It's located just above the city bank. There's plenty to learn there for those who are so inclined.
What is Sporehaven Karst?
Sporehaven Karst is home to the Circle of Spores. They're a group of reclusive druids who dedicate themselves to the research and proliferation of fungi.
Though normally quite harmless, their fungal research has a history of spreading infestations up into Faelindral, which we are then forced to cleanse.
Venture beneath the city to the caves that have been carved out by the river's passage, and pray that there's no sign of their latest experiments growing out of control.
If you do come across dangerous fungus, avoid it to the best of your ability while you search for evidence of the Circle's actions from the entrance of their domain.
And the ruined archway?
Disturbing rumors of the risen dead have made their way to Faelindral, particularly from the caravan route to the neighboring Keepers Bight.
Venture south, away from the river, and follow the main road toward the Bight. Just before you reach the border, you should see the ancient archway of Calafrey beneath a foot bridge.
See if you can find any evidence of an undead presence in the ruins, but don't engage them if the rumors prove true. Remember, you're only there to look this time around.
You receive Evidence of Orcs.
You receive Evidence of Nymphs.
You receive Evidence of Sporehaven.
You receive Scintillating Page.
An interesting method of procuring evidence, but I'll not scorn success. It seems my fears were not unfounded. I was right to send you to scout these locations.
You've shown that you can traverse the Weald and return with useful information, and that's what we need in our rangers. Here, you've earned this.
A good cloak on your shoulders is one of the basic tenants of wilderness survival. As an initiate of the Ardent Keepers, you'll be outdoors rather often.
Which leads us to your next assignment, initiate. You've seen the state of things in the Weald. Are you ready to help clean it up?
i am ready
I'm glad to hear it. Take some time to familiarize yourself more with the forest, then check back and I'll have something for you.
Greetings initiate, how fares the state of your cloak?
Im glad to hear it. You look as though you're familiar with the forest's trails by now. Allow me to see your initiate cloak one last time to make sure it's donned properly.
Excellent. Your next task begins immediately, initiate. Take this satchel.
Carry yourself down to the forest floor and eliminate some of the threats that you witnessed, particularly the undead, the roaming fae, and the orcish threat.
What Captain?
You're to venture south to Keepers Blight with your full satchel, and head toward the village of Penshaw. Follow the edge of the forest and cross the river, you should come upon one of our camps.
Ah, what brings you to Keepers Bight, initiate? Do you carry news from the Weald?
Undead of our ancestors in the Weald, as well as fae venturing out of their domain? This is disheartening news, but I can assure you they're not crossing the boundary from Keepers Bight, at least.

Return the belt to me after you've worked it in and I've had a time to speak with Caelen. Until then, you're free to explore the Weald and cull any threats. Be sure to keep that cloak as well, so others will recognize you as a Keeper.
Good. It seems you're looking more comfortable in the garb of a Keeper.
You'll require something with more protection than what an initiate cloak and a mere waistguard can afford you, if I'm to send you on your next task.
What task are you sending me on next?
The first thing you're required to do is reinforce the initiate cloak you were given. An initiate keeps their cloak for life, but the standard variation will only serve you for so long.
Bring your cloak to one of our senior trackers, Gareth Ashenpath. He should be outside the Rangers Rest and can guide you maintaining and improving your own equipment.
Let me guess, Relgen is delegating his responsibilities again? Doesn't surprise me.
The old man needs to spend more time down in the actual forest and less time berating potential rangers from the safety of the city, of you ask me.
Still, that doesn't mean I'm going to runaway an initiate like yourself. You're going to need to know how to enhance your cloak one way or another.
Yours in particular is in need of some real improvement.
Oh jeepers, what improvement can we do?
The flora of the Weald have been infused with magic over the course of many years. The preserved leaves we used aren't just protective, they're capable of adaption under the right circumstances.
The best way to improve your cloak, at least initially is to purposefully expose it to the same environmental effects that you wish it to protect you from. Make sense, right?

While you'll have to find ways of subverting every element at some point, for now, we'll focus on venom and poisons. The mountain snakes in the Bight and the vipers of Szuur can be deadly foes if they manage to inject you with some of their lethal venom.
You probably don't want to march all the way to the desert, though. Lucky for you, we have a critter on the forest floor than can you the proper... exposure.
By golly, what critter is that?
You've probably noticed out issue with the local drakeling population.
If left unchecked, they can overwhelm most of the Weald's younger fauna using their magical poison breath.
So what better way to expose you to poison than by having it breathe all over you, eh?
Go cull some of the drakelings and expose that cloak of yours to their poisonous breath.

Bring me back at least two of their hides and four drakeling scales as proof that you've been out there fighting the good fight. Oh, and your initiate cloak of course. We'll see then if you've exposed it to enough poison for it to adapt.

Granted the poison of a young drakeling is only so strong, but you also don't want to expose the cloak to too much and overwhelm it. You have to nurture it, just as you would an other plant of the forest.
I'll provide you with a salve that you can use to speed up the recovery process and lock in the magic of the drakeling's breath.

You can bring your cloak to a tanning vat to apply the salve. Make sure it's coated fully before returning it to me for inspection. You don't need to have any actual tanning skill, so don't worry about ruining your cloak.
Good, see here? The fivers of your cloak are starrting to weave together stronger than they once were. It should be more resilient to poison in general.
This is just one of the many gifts that we've been given by the forests of Evershade, and why its so important that we protect our home. We help the land and it helps us in turn.
Oh, and here. Take this as a gift from me. A lot of rangers like yourself might find it useful out in the Weald.
With this you may be capable of an important assignment, initiate.
What assignment?

We've recently received reports from the Wyrdguard scouts that orcs have encroached further into our territory than previously expected. As the protectors of our borders, this is an offense that we cannot ignore.

The Wyrdguard have already involved themselves in the effort to cull the orcish presence, and the Keepers will not be far behind. We know they have trackers which they employ to hunt innocent caravans on the route to Faelindral.

You're to hunt down their orc trackers before they manage to lay a finger upon an innocents. Eliminate as many as it takes to uncover who or what they might be reporting to, then bring back any evidence you find to me.
This is utter nonsense to my eyes. Thankfully, there's a researcher who's currently attempting to decipher the orcish language.
Bring the report to Researcher Fairgrove, who's likely poring over texts at the Heartwood Archives.
Find out if she can glean any meaning from these accursed scribbles.
O-oh, what's this? From an... o-orc tracker? Let me s-see what I can make out for you, K-Keeper.
Time... attack... orders. Foot-no, toes? Four. Four feet? Hmm... this is quite curious.
I, u-umm... I b-believe the report mentions something about an... an a-attack , and orders coming from s-someone names Fourth Feet? Or Four Toes.
Unfortunately that's a-all I can manage to decipher for now, but I... I hope that I was at least able to help in some regard, Keeper!
Hmm, four toes, you say? It's not much, but it does give me an idea.
If they're taking orders from someone named Four Toes, that might be all the information we need to track them down.

This would also serve a s good test of your abilities, Keeper. There can't be too many orcs within Evershade who have four toes, after all. Let's hope their naming conventions are as literal as they sound.
You'll need this for your important mission, Keeper.
What important mission?
While eliminating orc leaders is always warranted, there are times when capturing an enemy alive is more beneficial in a prolonged battle.

That powder I've given you was made from the mysterious foam you brought me during your initiation. You did well to bring me a sample. It has powerful hypnotic properties that we should be able to use to subdue the orc leader.
The only snag will be searching for the right... opportunity.
What opportunity?
Even orcs must sleep, so I propose you uncover the location of this leader's camp and wait until nightfall to subdue the four-toed beast while it slumbers.

It'd be wise to shroud yourself if you're to infiltrate the orc-controlled regions, though you'll have to avoid the undead presence if that the route you choose. They have sight for the soul rather than what's truly visible.
Approach the camp during the night to catch the leader while they sleep. Pour the dust onto them, and with any luck, you should be able to silently haul them back here for questioning.
If you lose or misplace the dust, you can ask me for more. If the orc proves to be resistant to the effects of the foam... you have my leave to eliminate them. Your life before theirs, Keeper.
It's unfortunate that you were unable to capture the commander alive, but this is still a great victory all the same.
We'll have more opportunities to question the orc leadership and discover their true intentions in the future. For now, I award with this spear as a sign of your accomplishment.
Carry it well, Almond, for you are an initiate no longer.
You are a full and true Ardent Keeper!

lines.text: Head to the Steel Talons Martial Academy on the Southwest side of Night Harbor and hand in your Notice of Recruitment to Fedamius Steel III
What is it?
Well, well... Foss has another aspiring Ranger on his hands. I wonder how long it'll be before he's out pulling you out of the sand?
The Rangers trained by the Steel Talons are the finest in the land, so you'll either become one of them or the next of your lot will use your corpse as a tracking exercise.
Now, take your note to Mister Dunestrider.
A skilled ranger needs no directions, so... you'll find him in one of the towers along the wall.
Bold text
Head to the top of the Wayfarer's Hospice north of the west gate and follow the top of the wall south until you find Foss Dunestrider above the west gate.
A new recruit, splendid. I know you're new to Night Harbor, but I'm sure you'll come to love this city as I do.
I've got some time, and I know you have at least a little skill from your experience outside these walls. So, let's see you in action. Take this tunic and head back down there.
As a test of your fieldcraft, I want you to collect the following...
a natural light source, butchered from a proximal creature...
a reagent harvested from a bat that might help you avoid a fall...
a venom gland, carefully removed from one of the younger snakes below...
and a Multhele Root.
You'll find all of these just outside our gates, with the exception of the root.
Head down to the noob yard below and kill a snakes, a fire beetles, and a desert bats
Hand Foss Dunestrider the Multhele Root, Immature Snake Venom Sac, Fire Beetle Eye, and Bat Wing
You looked good out there. And don't look surprised. Given that tunic, you weren't hard to track.
Excellent fieldcraft. A ranger's tricks of the trade mean the difference between life and death down range.
After watching you move around out there, you seem experienced or at least capable enough to assist me with a matter of personal interest.

The consensus in the garrison is that the Ashira are bothersome, but I think there's more to them than most assume. I think there's a sickness in them, but we've been unable to gather specifics. Maybe we can learn more by gathering information from other afflicted c reatures in the area.
I'd like you to carefully gather the blood of a diseased bat, rat, snake, and jackl. Seal the vials in this pack and return it to me when you're done.
Head to the cave entrance towards Wyrmsbane and kill a diseased bat, a diseased rat, a diseased snake, and a diseased jackal.

lines.text: Before entering the Bends portion of Night Harbor, climb the nearby gate stairs to find Lieutenant Jarovik Holt and Corporal Theodora. Holt is visibly distressed and requests you speak with Theodora.
Hail, Lieutenant Jarovik Holt.
Leave me be, citizen. Speak to my corporal, Theodora, if you want to make yourself useful.
Who is Theodora?
You will find the corporal in yonder hall. Move along now.
Hail, Corporal Theodora.
Mind how you go, citizen. I cannot guarantee your safety if you enter the Bends.
What are the Bends?
Riverbend is one of Night Harbor's oldest districts. It was once a vibrant fishing village and port of commerce, before the gangs took over.
What gangs?

There are three rival gangs in the Bends... the Ten Hooks, the Waterdogs, and the Serpent Sashes. We've contained the worst of them within these walls, but I'm afraid Night Harbor won't know peace until we've exterminated their kind.
Now leave me to my work, citizen, unless you wish to aid our great city.
I wish to aid our great city.

Know this, citizen, should you enter the Bends, you'll be met with violence. Meet with the Ten Hooks and Waterdogs in the dirty hovels they inhabit, and bring me proof of your valor. You'll be well rewarded.
Enter the Bends and begin killing the gang members residing there. These mobs will start non-KOS but will quickly become aggressive due to negative faction hits when killed.
Eventually, you will loot a Bloodied Allegiance Cuffs. Return to Corporal Theodora and hand her the cuffs.
The streets are safer for your efforts, citizen.
This can also be done with
which also drops from the local mobs and gives a small faction boost and 35 silver.

There are other notable named gang members directly inside the first area of the Bends, Karif Jamah, Tinka Roofstrider, Vikar Brask and Ratan. It is unclear if they have dialogue to continue this quest...
Hail, Ratan.
Hail yerself, mate. Standin' around... have you not got a job to do?
What job?
Ten Hooks are takin' liberties lately and we've given 'em enough chances. People don't learn if you don't explain it to 'em.
Who are the Ten Hooks?
Honest fishermen, so they say! As likely hook a fish as hook yer eyes out.
Those uppity thugs wear fancy cuffs like they're in a gentlemen's club or something. Bring me a pair and I'll give you a pretty penny.
It ain't pretty, but it does the job. Here you go, mate.
Hail, Karif Jamah.
Speak up, Human. These streets belong to the Ten Hooks. What's your business?
Business?
If your hands are idle, there's work that needs doing.
Work?
The Waterdogs have been useful to us, but they've become too bold.
Those pirates are fond of their jewelry. Collect four of their earrings and return them to me. Go now, remind them of their place.
Four coins for four souls. Our family thanks you.

lines.text: Read Anonymous Letter you start with as a new Rogue character
Give Anonymous Letter to Elyndiir Nightshade in the Lambent Lantern Inn. (behind Bank).
Looks like you were found out by Naery. Still, you seem to had made an impression on her, and that in itself is an accomplishment.
And now I'm to offer you a chance to prove yourself? I wish that girl would at least discuss things with me before sending prospects backstage. Here, take this.
You're really looking for an opportunity?
I'm always looking to exploit an opportunity!
You can start by making your way to the Traders Terrace and handing this letter to Myrielle Softglade.
Foreign trade has slowed lately and that makes for bad business. If Myrielle has an idea of what might be wrong, you're going to help her get to the bottom of it.
When you're done, come fill me in on what you find. And avoid stepping onto the stage when you leave, or the bards will start giving me a headache.
Hail, Myrielle Softglade
Fair shades to you, Rogue. How did I know you were a Rogue? Ha, don't worry, I just have an eye for these things.
Elyn sent you? No offense, but I was hoping she'd send one of her more experienced agents.
Ah, it's no matter. Here, take this. Maybe you'd be able to help with a little... experiment?
Sample Jar
Wyrd's way, this is revolting! Quick, take it! Take it back!
Yes. Who is your contact?
Sylwine Brightspirit is a good friend of mine who's always looking for new reagents for her potions at the Well of Order. She said she'd be willing to take a look at anything that I brought her.
Of course, we don't really need any potions, but that's beside the point. If anything is wrong with those samples, she should be able to figure it out!
I just hope she doesn't mind the foul stench...
Myrielle sent you here with this, did she? Here, take it back for a moment. I'd like you to do something for me first.
I want you to open that jar for me and take a good whiff. Really let is invade your nasal passage. Then, tell me what you think it smells like.
Here's the receipt for the job. You can bring it back to Myrielle. This is going to take me a while, because of the contamination. That foolish girl...
She may be pretty and knows all the right words, but she's still two flowers short of a bouquet, if you catch my meaning.
In fact, you can tell her I said as much when you return to her!
A-ah, I... I see. Ahem. Well, it seems that we may have to wait a while to find out the results. You've proven that you're capable of some simple tasks, at least!
Here's a note for Elyn at the Willows Whisper. I'm sure that she can find something to keep you busy while we wait on Sylwine's tests.
I hope that she isn't too upset...
So Myrielle is having Sylwine run tests on some animal parts? I suppose that's one angle we hadn't considered.
We had you tailed during your journey to see how you'd perform. You're a little dull around the edges, but I feel like we could hone you into a fine agent.
Speaking of...
Any prospect of ours needs to be able to defend themselves. You earned it, but you could also earn a lot more. You interested?
Of course, I'm interested!
Hmm, not so fast. Why don't you get a little more practice with that dagger first? Come back and show me the blade once you've had a chance to put it through its paces.
I'm still interested.
Glad to hear it. Though let me get a look at that prospect dagger of yours first to make sure that it's been properly worked in.
Looks sufficiently worked-in to me, prospect. Good.
Ah, so Elyndir finally found time to send me an assistant? I've been requesting aid for weeks and I'm at my wits end when it comes to these capricious creatures!
What is the plan, then?
IS IT WORKING? CAN YOU HEAR ME?
Of course, I'm interested!
I'm willing. Sounds like fun!
Someone was out there... wasn't there?
There's no one there, Lilika, look! Now tell me your idea!
We can't be too careful with that Ereldian guy snooping around! You know he's just itching to punish us.
You mean he isn't just itching from the glitter you slipped into his pants?
Now out with it! I'm dying to hear your plan!
You won't be the only one dying! I noticed a weak spot in the cliffside near the road. Wouldn't it be funny if a whole caravan got trapped under a landslide?
Oh, wow! Would they know it was us?
They'd probably just blame those dumb orcs! They hate them a lot more than they hate us.
It'd be even better if we could drop rocks on that Ereldian.
You mean Smelldian?
Now take a nap! You spent the whole day drinking mushroom dew. I'm going to take a walk and check on that cliff.
If you decide to kill Lilika Thinsticks
HEY, WHO ARE YOU?!
I didn't... mean to...
Haha-ha! You've done all of the Weald a fantastic service for this!
That creature was nothing more than a conniving murderer. You've done the right thing. Perhaps I'll finally be able to sleep in peach tonight.
My thanks, friend. You'll go far if you keep this up. Here, take this.
You've earned it. Keep it close by. It may be of use to you in the future, should we require more of your... services.
Before running back
Myrielle, concerning the samples you had delivered... blah, blah, blah... clear signs of contamination... ooh, that sounds ominous! ...Resulted in a failure on your part due to...
What beasts?
And the option is?
May I see your blade as well as the fang? I want to offer a prayer to poor creature that lost its mind to madness.
Yes, the madness was unsettling!
Alashore, forgive us for being unable to protect one of the forest's mas souls. Their life had to be cut short in exchange for the lives of your servants.
The wasps, also.
Then there were those pups, too...
I, umm... I'm not particularly reverent. Are you? I'm sure the gods don't mind, since they're all sleeping anyway!
Take this note back to Elyn for me. We should hopefully be seeing a bit more trade with the roads kept clear. Thanks again for all your work, Villette!
I don't really agree with Myrielle's choice of action, but hopefully this sorts out our trade problem. Well done.
I feel like you've dealt with enough of our more... interesting members, Villette. If you've stuck around with us for this long, then you can probably be trusted with some more involved work.
Here, take this.
This may help you keep some anonymity during your next mission, though you may need to work on your skills before then.
Return to me and show me that blade of yours once you've strengthened your technique enough to incapacitate a foe,
A quarrel?
You may be familiar with the human village out in Keepers Bight known as Penshaw.
They call it one of their kontors, or trade posts, which means there hav been a number of new trade deals offered by the factions of Night Harbor in recent days.

The Iron Emissaries in particular are an arm of the human race that is notorious for their greed. What I need you to do is travel to Penshaw and determine whether one of their latest trade envoys is legitimate.
There's one sure way that you'll be able to make that determination.
What way will I determine that?
You'll do what we do best, prospect. Spy.

Rather than rouse suspicion by hailing every person you come across, I want you to venture into the village undetected and try to overhear any conversations regarding a new trade envoy from Night Harbor.
The tavern might be your best bet, as that's where gossip can get a little more candid.

If you manage to sniff out where this envoy is staying, you'll want to sneak into their dwelling and politely browse through their belongings without anyone noticing. It might be wise to wait until nightfall when they're asleep to do so.

You're looking for any sort of paper trail. Ledgers, receipts, or anything of the sort to verify their trade dealings, Copy anything you find onto the blank parchment I gave you, then return it to me.
Oh, and no violence, prospect. Not unless I determine that a message needs to be sent.
Oh good, a lesson!
Of course, I'm ready to hear the plan!
